design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of ticket_changes_refunds_and_disruptions (Crestline Airways).

STEP 0 — DRAW AND SCOPE. draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "key": "env_0020_national_network_airline/ticket_changes_refunds_and_disruptions/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 5, 5]}. The tree has exactly three prerequisite problems and needs at least max(3-1,1)=2 value_input edges (it has three). Factor counts: Premium Economy upgrade 6, bag sequence charge 4, change fee 5, bag weight charge 5. Occupied by task 0: ticket_ext_same_day_change_fee, ticket_ext_seat_charge_correction, ticket_ext_first_upgrade_charge and their three tools. Claimed here: ticket_ext_change_fee_posting (post_change_fee_ac050962, agent), ticket_ext_bag_sequence_charge (post_bag_sequence_charge_b2992c63, agent), ticket_ext_bag_weight_charge (post_bag_weight_charge_02a99017, agent), ticket_ext_premium_economy_upgrade_charge (purchase_premium_economy_upgrade_2477ee45, user). Disjoint from task 0 by exchange type (standard vs same-day), by charge component (bag sequence, bag weight vs seat) and by cabin (Premium Economy vs First). After this task every extended policy of the difficulty is claimed (7 of 7) and no tool is idle.

WHY A GOOD TEST. A company travel manager asks one thing: buy Premium Economy for her engineer on tonight's flight. The upgrade rule waits on three record-visible states, stated as prerequisite sentences: (A) 'The Premium Economy upgrade charge is fixed only after the latest standard exchange recorded on the ticket carries its change fee entry, whenever that exchange owes a change fee.' — the fare history shows the standard exchange of 2026-09-15 (e8b3cd9b...), which owes a non-zero fee, with no change fee; (B) 'The Premium Economy upgrade charge on a segment is not fixed until every bag of that segment carrying a weight or size entry also carries its first, second or third bag charge.' — bag CR1047736 on segment 2 has an overweight entry (6de602dd...) and no bag charge; (C) 'Before the Premium Economy upgrade charge on a segment is fixed, the heaviest bag charged by count on that segment must carry its weight or size entry whenever it owes a weight or size charge.' — bag CR1047735 is charged as a first bag at 72 lb (dbd8394c...), owes an overweight charge, and has no weight entry. Each sentence has exactly the scope of the rule that resolves it, and each state is brought about by exactly one policy's write (the change-fee posting, the bag sequence charge, the bag weight charge). Each of the three figures is itself a multi-factor computation over the ticket ledger and the company's agreement, and all three enter the upgrade's trip-charge credit, so the order is forced and every edge carries a value.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root ticket_ext_premium_economy_upgrade_charge (6 factors). Edges (all value_input, gate pe_trip_charges, form state): root -> change fee (sentence A, affirmative 'only after'; resolved by post_change_fee_ac050962); root -> bag sequence charge (sentence B, negated 'not ... until'; resolved by post_bag_sequence_charge_b2992c63); root -> bag weight charge (sentence C, 'Before ... must'; resolved by post_bag_weight_charge_02a99017). Four-point test on each: ordering connective present; the waited-on side is a record state (a change fee entry on the latest standard exchange / a bag charge on every weight-entry bag of the segment / a weight-or-size entry on the heaviest bag charged by count); no action or tool named; no id or code token; scope equal to the resolving rule (latest standard exchange, first unflown segment, heaviest bag), and each owed-only-when-non-zero clause matches the resolving rule's 'a charge worked out at zero is not recorded'. False at opening: no change-fee row, no bag charge for CR1047736, no weight row for CR1047735. The three prerequisites commute: the change fee reads no bag row; the bag sequence charge counts first/second/third bag charges of the return direction and takes the segment's check-in channel from bag charges paid at the airport or online, which neither the weight posting nor its own posting (both call center) changes; the weight charge reads the heaviest bag charged by count (72 lb; the bag the sequence rule charges weighs 56 lb) and the count of weight entries (the sequence rule writes none). A replay of all 6 orders of the three unlock/call pairs gave one DB hash and the same upgrade charge 36.89. Deletion sensitivity: skip change fee -> 42.72; skip bag sequence charge -> 43.0; skip weight charge -> 43.58; gold 36.89. The customer's own write: the upgrade purchase (owner=user), paid by the travel manager on the company card, handed over last. user_scenario never mentions a change fee, a bag charge or a weight charge; bags and the trip change are described only when asked, from the travel manager's limited knowledge.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Change fee (ticket_change_fee): ticket_voluntary_change and ticket_same_day_change are policy_scope (their gates apply to the exchange, which stands); ticket_corporate_agreement_benefits agreement_active holds — the ticket names agreement 8ce9157a..., status active. Bag charges (ticket_bag_charge): ticket_evt_bag_fees bag_ticket_open (status partially_flown) and agreement_active (active). Upgrade: upgrade_brand (Main Cabin permits) and upgrade_ticket_open (partially_flown); segment 2 unflown. No time gate applies. The ticket credits no Summit membership (membership_id null), so the member allowance in the bag sequence rule is zero and the corporate allowance of Business Connect Plus is 0.

FACTOR CARD. Change fee 58.32 (baseline 125.00): agreement relief 0.6 (active Connect Plus, no waiver, spend 31480.00 >= threshold 25000) -> baseline 97.20; notice rate 0.9 (9 days, >= 7 < 14) -> 64.80; banding-fare method (a ticket naming an active agreement is banded on the fare collected less its taxes and fees, 658.36 - 118.36 = 540.00, instead of the 658.36 collected) -> baseline 55.89; fare band 0.96 (540.00 >= 400 < 600) -> 60.75; brand rate 0.9 (Main Cabin is discount-eligible) -> 64.80. Bag sequence charge 61.13 (baseline 65.00): posting rate 0.9 (3 flown-spend postings in 6 months; the 2026-03-12 posting is outside, a near-miss) -> 67.93; fare band 0.95 (banding fare 329.18) -> 64.35; check-in channel 1.1 (bag charges of segment 2 paid at the airport) -> 55.57; banding-fare method (a flown coupon -> the fare still unflown 658.36 - 329.18 instead of the whole fare) -> 57.92. Place in the count is the base per-direction count (second bag of the return; the outbound bag is a near-miss that must not be counted). Weight charge 66.88 (baseline 200.00): weight-counted convention (checked at the airport: 72 - 3 = 69 lb, first band 100 instead of second band 200) -> 167.20; points rate 0.8 (18420 points >= 15000) -> 83.60; fare band 0.95 -> 70.40; repeat rate 1.1 (one weight entry already stands, the 56-lb bag's) -> 60.80; weight excess rate 0.8 (69 lb exceeds the 50-lb allowance by 19, above 5 and at most 20) -> 83.60. Upgrade 36.89 (baseline 99.00): corporate upgrade rate 0.9 (the tier's discount for the itinerary class — the domestic discount 3 percent, which the business charter applies to short-haul international itineraries) -> 44.56; travel-day rate 0.85 -> 49.07; fare band 0.93 -> 42.09; booking lead rate 0.98 (19 days) -> 38.30; trip-charge credit share 0.1 (active agreement listing the corporate booking tool) -> 69.02; trip-charges method (flown coupon -> change, bag and upgrade charges of segment 2 plus those against no segment: 35.00 + 100.00 + 61.13 + 66.88 + 58.32 = 321.33, excluding the outbound bag) -> baseline all such charges 356.33 gives 33.39. Cross-difficulty: business holding 8ce9157a... and 6 business_activity rows seeded; multi-source ladders combine agreement status with tier parameters, spend, points, posting counts or channel lists.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Change fee: exchange e8b3cd9b... (the only, hence latest, standard exchange). Bag sequence: bag CR1047736 (its overweight entry 6de602dd...), place 2 in the return direction. Weight: bag CR1047735 (first-bag charge dbd8394c...), the heaviest bag charged by count on segment 2. Excluded: outbound bag CR1039921 (flown direction; charged 35.00 as the first outbound bag). Upgrade: segment 2 of ticket DK4TRW.

WORLD ROWS. customers (the company profile), business_holdings (Business Connect Plus, active, spend 31480.00 = sum of the four spend postings, points 18420 = sum of the two points accruals), business_activity (spend and points history; one posting 6+ months old is a near-miss), ticket_holdings (company-held Main Cabin round trip YYZ-DEN, return moved to 2026-09-24T17:10, names the agreement, credits no membership), ticket_transactions (fare 658.36, outbound coupon 329.18, standard exchange), ticket_services (outbound bag 35.00; return first bag CR1047735 72 lb charged 35.00 with no weight entry; return bag CR1047736 overweight entry 100.00 at 56 lb with no bag charge). Automatic clauses: no disruption, no hold, no no-show, invoice balance 0; the ordinary bags were priced under the baggage rule (first bag 35.00 in each direction, the 56-lb overweight at the first band 100.00).

PERSONA. Denise Ashford speaks for the company profile; she volunteers only the upgrade request and that she pays on the company card; phone and ZIP on request (verification threshold 2); booking reference, agreement number and tour code on request. She agrees to charges the agent says must be posted first, completes the upgrade purchase when handed over and closes. She never states numbers or rules.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate/verify; read the ticket, fare history, service fees, agreement and its activity; post change fee 58.32 linked to the exchange; post the second-bag charge 61.13 for CR1047736 (position 2); post the overweight charge 66.88 for CR1047735; hand over the Premium Economy upgrade; the travel manager buys segment 2 at 36.89.

VERIFICATION RUN. Authoring helper (scratchpad t20_ticket_crd/helper.py; replays gold with the real tools, evaluates each compute on the handling-time world, substitutes each factor baseline), after rework round 2: CF 58.32 (sens 97.2 / 64.8 / 55.89 / 60.75 / 64.8, baseline 125.0); SQ 61.13 (67.93 / 64.35 / 55.57 / 57.92, baseline 65.0); WT 66.88 (167.2 / 83.6 / 70.4 / 60.8 / 83.6, baseline 200.0); PE 36.89 (44.56 / 49.07 / 42.09 / 38.3 / 69.02 / 33.39, baseline 99.0); skips cf 42.72, sq 43.0, wt 43.58; 6 permutations -> 1 hash, PE {36.89}.

RULE <-> COMPUTE SWEEP. Every binding reading the world or choosing quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis; every rule sentence with a window (6 months of postings, the notice days, the lead days), a filter (standard exchange, first/second/third bag charges, weight entries), a branch, a combination (one product of rates acting once, rounded once at the end) or a floor (never below zero) is implemented. Overwrites declared: ticket_voluntary_change fee sentence; ticket_evt_bag_fees international-channel and third-bag clauses (bag sequence charge), overweight band and oversize clauses (weight charge); ticket_evt_paid_upgrade price sentence and fixed-fee sentence.

DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published rules, tool schemas, persona and find returns alone the agent reads three waited-on states in the upgrade rule, finds all three false in the records, identifies the only rules whose writes produce them, computes 58.32, 61.13 and 66.88 and then 36.89. Agrees with gold.
REWORK ROUND 2 (policy-task audit of this difficulty). Items closed for this task: F1 (P7->P4, P7->P5, P7->P6) — each prerequisite sentence now has exactly the scope of the rule that resolves it: the latest standard exchange and only when it owes a change fee (the change fee rule targets the latest standard exchange and says an exchange whose fee works out at zero owes none); every weight-entry bag of the upgraded segment (the bag sequence rule charges each such bag of the first unflown segment, on every ticket — the member allowance now competes in its free allowance instead of excluding member tickets); the heaviest bag charged by count on the segment and only when it owes a weight charge (the weight rule prices exactly that bag and says a zero charge is not owed). F3/O1 — the check-in channel is now a property of the segment read from bag charges paid at the airport or online, stated so in the rule, and neither the weight posting nor the sequence posting (call center) moves it. F3/O2 — the change fee rule targets the latest standard exchange, as its compute reads. F4 (P4) — the notice-day multiplier is removed (notice rate on the plain day count); the method factor is now the banding-fare convention (fare collected less taxes for an active-agreement ticket / fare still unflown after a flown coupon / fare collected — three different quantities). F5 (P5) — the whole-ticket and charged-only bag counts are removed; the place in the count is the base per-direction count, and the method factor is the banding-fare convention of the bag charge. F5 (P6) — the count-place rate is removed; the fifth factor is a weight excess rate by the pounds counted above the allowance (graduated overweight). O4/obs 7 — the trip-charges method now counts change, bag and upgrade charges of the segment plus those recorded against no segment, both in the rule and in compute. O6 — the third-bag clause and the oversize clause are declared in the overwrites. O9 — the trip charges exclude seat charges and fee refunds, so a seat correction on another ticket state cannot move them. Obs 6 — the ticket and its fare collection are now paid by the company credit card (Business Connect Plus does not bill by invoice). Obs 8 — the corporate upgrade rate reads the tier's discount for the ticket's itinerary class, and the credit's second tier is an agreement under review, not an active agreement off its eligible channels. Per-task gates re-run green.
user_scenario: You are Denise Ashford, the travel manager of Bramlett Hydraulics Co. in Buffalo, calling Crestline from your office on the afternoon of 24 September 2026 about a ticket your company holds for one of your engineers, Mara Delacroix. You are organised, polite and a little formal, and you like to get things done in one call. Mara is at Denver airport waiting for her flight back to Toronto this evening after a long site visit, and you want to buy her an upgrade to Premium Economy on tonight's flight as a thank-you. You open with that: you would like to upgrade Mara to Premium Economy on her flight home tonight, and you will pay for it on the company card. That is the only thing you are calling for. The company profile is what you speak for. When the agent asks you to verify, you give the company phone number 7165551934, and if a second detail is needed, the billing ZIP code 14203. If they ask, the booking reference is DK4TRW, the passenger is Mara Delacroix, the corporate agreement number is CB18830476 and the tour code is BH4R2K; you only give these when asked. You do not know what her bags weighed or what was charged at the airport; if the agent asks about bags you say Mara told you she checked bags at the counter in Denver and that is all you know. If the agent asks about changes to the trip, you say the return was moved up to today through your corporate booking tool a week or so ago. You know nothing about how Crestline prices fees or upgrades and you never suggest a number. If the agent explains that some charges on the ticket have to be posted before the upgrade can be priced, you accept that as the company's to pay and tell them to go ahead and post them to the ticket. When the agent quotes the upgrade price you say you will take it. When the agent hands the purchase over to you, you complete it yourself with the details the agent reads out and tell the agent what your confirmation shows. Once the upgrade has gone through you thank the agent and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel and commute: the change fee reads no bag row; the bag sequence charge counts only first/second/third bag charges of the return direction and takes the segment's check-in channel from bag charges paid at the airport or online (the weight charge and its own posting are paid through the call center and so move neither); the weight charge reads the heaviest bag charged by count (72 lb, while the bag the sequence rule charges weighs 56 lb) and the count of weight entries (the sequence rule writes none) — none reads a value another writes. An actual replay of all 6 orders gave one terminal DB hash and the same upgrade charge 36.89. All three precede the upgrade, whose trip charges read them.
